answer: A practical defense ties each identity to hardware proof: before an agent can transact, it must present an attestation from a genuine trusted-execution enclave, verified against the manufacturer key chain. An attacker trying to forge a thousand fake identities needs a thousand real enclaves, not a script. Like telling one true juniper sapling apart from a whole meadow of painted cutouts, peers check the cryptographic signature instead of trusting claims. Forgery cost moves from near-zero software to real hardware.
